_README: Hand-authored STRUCTURE for the generated history (docs/history.html). The generator (tools/build-history.js) derives ALL dates, commit lists, ADRs and cart-birth data from git + index.json — this file only supplies what a parser can't infer: era boundaries, subsystem identity + matchers, importance tiers, the marked days, and the (mostly empty) editorial seam. Editorial prose, when written, follows docs/guides/voice.md. Re-run: `node tools/build-history.js`. Scope: weeks 1–10 (through 2026-07-30). COVERAGE: all three layers now span the full window. `eras` + `markedDays` are complete; `observations` are refreshed to 2026-07-30 (see their `asOf`); and `milestones` were backfilled 2026-07-11→07-30 on 07-30 (175 entries, taking the total to 384), so a per-subsystem or per-tier TALLY finally describes the whole window rather than the repo through 07-10. Two things that backfill taught, worth heeding before the next one: (1) verify every `match` resolves to a commit INSIDE its declared era before trusting it — the generator picks the FIRST (oldest) subject containing the string, so a short matcher like 'mic' silently grabbed a week-1 commit, and 7 of 175 were wrong on the first pass, including two whose era was genuinely a day off in the prose; and (2) a backfill INVALIDATES older observations that quote milestone counts — eight evidence lines and one body had to be corrected, and one observation's central claim reversed once its window was measured on the same basis as the rest.
title: dreamengine — a history
subtitle: How a fantasy console grew, week by week. Built structure-first from git, the STATUS ledger, and the decision log.

eras.title: Bootstrap — "get a window open"
eras.blurb: Ported from the sibling 'eventually' studio and renamed to dreamengine. One evening: editor chrome (Makefile, clipboard, tabs), assets embedded straight into the binary, a Windows cross-compile — capped at 23:55 by a single 'big batch' commit that drops the first sound system and the map editor.

eras.title: The API sprint
eras.blurb: A research braindump (Scratch / Strudel / Dilla) feeds two days of rapid-fire primitives and helpers. The cart pipeline forms (make-cart, tutorials, save/load), the web build lands (emscripten + a Build-for-Web button), and the first real synth arrives (ADSR / duty / LFO / resonant filter). The docs get reorganised by genre and the decision log is born.

eras.title: Rigor & tooling
eras.blurb: Less new surface, more correctness. Camera transforms, arc/ring primitives, and a hard rasterization-consistency push (one coverage test for circ/oval/tri/rrect). The debug harness lands — deterministic record/replay/script/trace. Fifty carts arrive at once via parallel Workflow batches. Geometry helpers, physics sketches, and fade() made immediate-mode.

eras.title: Subsystems are born
eras.blurb: The pivotal stretch. In two days: the profiler, dreamcad (a 3D model editor), held notes (note_on/off), modrack (a modular synth, steps 0→6, plus a module zoo), and the libtcc live backend (cart-as-script, de_state, hot-reload). The navkit instrument-port spec is written — it seeds the entire June sound saga — and mod-envelopes give the synth its second EG.

eras.title: Sound tools & the first stations
eras.blurb: The SFX editor and slider-driven generator land, plus drawable single-cycle waveforms (wave_set / INSTR_USER) and sample-accurate scheduling (schedule_hit). The first generative radio stations appear — bossa, ambient, jangle, lowend — and the cart taxonomy gets its capstones (the collision, movement and steering clusters). A dropped-request tripwire makes the sound queue trustworthy.

eras.title: Roland machines & the radio explosion
eras.blurb: The densest day yet. The Roland drum-machine family is synthesized from measured analog circuit values — CR-78, TR-808, TB-303, TR-909 — and a dozen radio stations pour out (city pop, dub, house, satie, tango, exotica, yacht, roadhouse, cocktail, ymo). radio.h is extracted as the shared station chassis, the first navkit port engines arrive (PLUCK, MALLET, FM), drive and echo become the first bus effects, and THE BAND panel + the improviser (improv.h) give the stations players.

eras.title: Mobile, widgets & the first keyboards
eras.blurb: A breather, then tooling. touch_ceiling() and the mobile worklist land, plus a debug overlay. ui.h ships a cross-input widget kit — button/slider/knob for mouse, touch and keyboard at once. The first keyboard instruments arrive (INSTR_ORGAN, INSTR_EPIANO) alongside teaching carts: flappy, the smallest complete game, and whatiscode, lesson zero.

eras.title: The engine-port marathon
eras.blurb: The navkit instrument ports land in a row until every modeled timbre exists: the envelope follower (a third modulation source), PD, REED (blown waveguide), PIPE (jet flute), GUITAR + PIANO (verbatim StifKarp), BOWED (Smith/McIntyre stick-slip), and finally BRASS — the last engine. Audio goes stereo (instrument_pan / LFO_PAN), the solo.h jam layer lets the player solo over a station, and the formant filter is specced.

eras.title: The effects cookbook & true colour
eras.blurb: The §8.10 effects roster completes: per-instrument chorus/flanger (effects on one instrument, not the whole mix), tape (wow/flutter/saturation), and the long-promised auto-wah — the 'scar' finally resolved as a bus effect. Drive modes and bitcrush ship too. On the graphics side, true-colour pixels arrive — pset_rgb / rectfill_rgb / pget_rgb — powering CPU shader carts.

eras.title: The mixing console & MIDI
eras.blurb: The engine becomes a real mixing console: a reorderable insert chain (fx_order), a multi-reverb tank pool, sidechain + bus compression (glue), a swept filter, and auto-pan. Then it learns to listen — engine-level MIDI keyboard input (CoreMIDI native, Web MIDI in the browser) plus keybed.h, a shared polyphonic keybed seven carts migrate onto. Audits (mono/poly, keycap) and the spline road world (roadnet) round out the stretch.

eras.title: Spatial audio
eras.blurb: Positional audio in two layers, one day. v1: a listener() + positioned voices give automatic pan, distance-volume and Doppler (the OpenAL model in 2D pixel space). v2: emitter buses move a whole effected source as one object, so its reverb/shimmer tail pans and Dopplers with it. The library also crosses its scale milestones — 14 MACRO engines, 32 simultaneous voices.

eras.title: Roads, stealth & engine tuning
eras.blurb: Attention turns to the big sims and the long tail of polish. The deterministic spline road world grows up — roadlab (lane-accurate roads + clothoid joints), interchange (a data-driven junction matrix), rampkit — and flank, a tactical stealth-squad game, takes real shape (fog of war, suppression, reaction time, an ammo economy). A street-level fill language starts underneath the roads (lotfill). On the audio side the waveguide top-octave tuning is finally fixed (PLUCK/REED/BRASS), a generalized all-engine tuner lands, and the first stability gates show up — level-check and fx-check, the start of a guard-rail suite.

eras.title: Junctions, jobs & guard-rails
eras.blurb: The longest day in the window, and a quiet turn in what the project is about. roadlab stops faking roads and becomes a real geometry engine — junctions described as a table of lane-links straight off the OpenDRIVE model, the trumpet/fork/triangle topology family, ring roads, loop and S-curve ramps, all generated from a type instead of placed by hand. Next to it a new kind of cart appears: thecut and handwork aren't games or instruments, they're production sims — what a worker costs, when it's worth hiring one, what an hour of your own hands is worth against a machine's. That's the second north star — deep honest sims under a lo-fi surface — made literal. And the whole engine grows guard-rails the same day: a suite of stability gates (effect-stacking, long-run soak, wasm-vs-native parity), the web pitch bug finally pinned and fixed (48k devices had been playing everything ~147 cents sharp), DC-blocked feedback loops, and a first real optimization pass on the fill rasterizer.

eras.title: Rebuilding the Moog, late
eras.blurb: A quiet late-night start to the week, all synth. moog is torn down and rebuilt as a proper 3-oscillator Model D with a real ladder filter (FILTER_LADDER), and onenote — a one-note funk groovebox — lands beside it. A null-result probe (pset draw-call batching, native + WebGL) gets captured rather than thrown away. The deepening that fills the next day starts here.

eras.title: One day, four fronts
eras.blurb: The single biggest day in the project's history — around 145 commits — and four threads advance at once, in parallel. (1) The synth grows up: oscillator hard sync, the Steiner-Parker multimode filter, and a flood of liveset playthings (euclid, turing, dubsiren, lpg, dubdesk, easel) and artist/genre radio stations (eno, plantasia, squarepusher fm, plaid fm, wba, the xx, afrobeat, vapor, lofi) — with ADR 0019 deciding the oscillators stay naive. (2) The project learns to read itself: cart-index.js and the TEACHES/LINEAGE convention, the spec() cart-logic harness, the ★ techniques compendium in the editor, teaches[] becoming a required index.json field behind a controlled-vocabulary gate, plus cart-dupes.js and teaching-gaps.md. (3) The at-grade streets: streetlab runs M1→M7 and a lane-section refactor — curb returns, T-junctions, turn lanes, the street web, sidewalks/crosswalks, the mini-roundabout, the typed OpenDRIVE cross-section, bike lanes and bulb-outs — the at-grade sibling of roadlab, spec-locked. (4) The turn toward a larger game: the clip+reel pipeline (clips carry audio; compose-clips stitches reels), the showreel-teaser note, and a wave of game carts — facegen (procedural street portraits + conversation), runecrawl (circuit-dungeon), beltworks (Factorio-lite), boom — plus cards.h, cursor.h and the 04b-mouse tutorial.

eras.title: The city wakes up
eras.blurb: It opens at midnight like a closing — boom ships as an explosion-and-fire sandbox, the week's carts go live in one big site publish (boom, 04b-mouse, beltworks, facegen, logic, runecrawl, streetlab), streetlab and facegen get end-of-session resume notes. Then the day turns into the opposite of a closing: three city sims wake up at once and run all day. gridcity is a SimCity in miniature — a data-layer sim where land value, crime, pollution, power, water and fire feed back on each other, grown from a v1 to a real RCI-demand city in an afternoon. cityplan merges lotfill and building interiors into one procedural town under a zoom-banded roof lift. trackgen's cars stop racing and start living — traffic mode, jams, a light, collisions that express each driver's mass. boom keeps growing teeth: destructible walls, ram cars, pedestrians, dithered smoke. And streetlab reaches its Stage-2 superblock with a circuity metric. A whole world to drive through, built between one midnight and the next.

eras.title: Down to the pixels
eras.blurb: The day the renderer got interrogated. The big one: the software-canvas investigation finally RUNS, and comes back GO — rasterize the whole frame on the CPU into a byte-identical framebuffer and cityplan drops from 11.4ms to 5.0ms a frame. Phases 0 through 2 land in a row (cbuf + UpdateTexture, then spr/print/tritex/span-fills as CPU blits, then camera zoom in software with rotation falling back to the GPU), and the win is honestly scoped — it's a pset-bound win, not a universal one. Underneath it, a determinism question gets chased to the floor: the det-probes prove rotated fills, strokes and sprites are gap-free and reproducible, RotSprite (EPX ×3) goes head-to-head and wins on lines but not lone specks, and cross-arch libm trig drift gets quantized away. The roads got a big chunk of their own. Field-based road rendering — the long-queued refactor that draws a road from a per-pixel lateral-coverage field instead of stamped quads — finally lands, shipped opt-in behind the road-check oracle (framebuffer invariants: no naked edges, no strays, no floating kerb at any angle) and blessed by ADR 0021 (the geometry lives in plain 2D; the pseudo-3D view is just a rendering adapter). cityview puts a GTA1-ish four-mode camera over the world and folds the overpass raised-flyover experiment into itself, and trackgen's traffic learns cross-roads, right-of-way reservations, K-turns and police chases.

eras.title: The city, loaded for real
eras.blurb: The roads stopped being a sandbox and became a place. roadview learns a packed binary format (.rvb) so tens of megabytes of OpenStreetMap load in under a second, its pools grow to fit ALL of Amsterdam (~4.2M points / 575k ways), and it stops sampling and pulls the FULL ladder of the data — every road class, hashed understory, multipolygon water, and SimCity-style zoning layers (landuse / rail / sand) with outlined building footprints. An absolute zoom ceiling lets a whole city zoom down to street detail. The cart loads its world at runtime, so you swap cities by swapping a file — no regen — and cityview gets published to the gallery. The groundwork for driving a real city.

eras.title: It runs on the phone
eras.blurb: The iOS port crossed from spikes to the real thing. Phase 2 lands: the actual studio.c + sound.h — the real engine, zero Raylib via the DE_NO_RAYLIB seam — renders omnichord pixel-correct and sounds it through CoreAudio on a real iPhone, UIKit touch driving it. The AUv3 extension stops hosting a stand-in and hosts the REAL engine as a sample-clocked sequencer, then takes host MIDI so it's a playable instrument rack inside other apps. The load-bearing renderer question gets settled and written down — ADR-0024: the software canvas is canonical for 2D (no ANGLE on iOS); 3D stays GPU-only and off the initial list — after on-device FPS is measured (2D carts hold 59–60fps; tritex ~10fps). A perf harness logs frames to the Documents dir. Nothing left to set up; device work just runs here now.

eras.title: The tools turn on themselves
eras.blurb: A multi-track day whose headline was the project turning its tools on itself. The knowledge layer: build-context gathers one cart's scattered docs, its horizontal twin topic-brief assembles a feature dossier across the whole repo, and lint-xrefs finds the docs that should cross-link but don't (432 missing backlinks → 42 once it learns to spot domain hubs by in-degree). Then the views — design-board reads every design doc's STATUS line into a lifecycle board (the ★ todo page, styled as a lo-fi Comic-Mono console checklist), and build-reflections turns the field-notes journal into the ★ reflections page beside it, both over a shared doc-status.js that owns the phase vocabulary. The rest of the day is honesty passes against those views: triage 29 unmarked design docs, relocate 5 misplaced field-notes, migrate carts' hidden prose todos into de:meta.todo[], wire the 260-cart-todo backlog onto the board, and — the closing move — audit all 15 field notes against the repo and record on each what it actually became (the journal flips from 10 observed / 0 incorporated to 10 incorporated). In parallel: citydrive turns the loaded city into a drivable pseudo-3D world — real metre-scaled car, mouse orbit/zoom, terrain elevation off a DEM, water and mountains around the edges, a pitched perspective camera — and a '📱 to iPhone' button lands in the editor to deploy the live cart to a connected device.

eras.title: A road grammar, a paint studio, and touch everywhere
eras.blurb: The last day of the week runs on four fronts at once. The roads get a shared grammar: roadkit.h is declared GO — connectivity FIRST, markings later — and citydrive becomes its first consumer, rendering Delft as one connected asphalt surface with OSM-driven lane markings and carriageway width, on-road cycle lanes (fietsstrook), canals drawn under the roads, raised bridge decks and dashed tunnels. sloop starts actually driving the real city — P1 rungs A→C wire road_at() over a real-Delft spatial index, render the OSM world, let the surface drive handling, and crash into real buildings; drag a .rvb and you drive a real place. squishy turns into a painting studio — a SELECT tool grows through three stages into a per-stroke vector editor (pick → highlight → edit properties), joined by drip / calligraphy / oil / rotation brushes, a per-stroke outline and a bevel 'sun' you can angle, colour and spin, two boil styles, CMY colours and z-order. And touch controls generalize to N action buttons (an A/B/X/Y diamond, 0–4) with TOUCH_DPAD4/DPAD8 move modes, a scale-to-fit band and a debug introspection API — then get swept across ~16 existing carts in a single pass (boids, doomfire, defender, galaga, vampire, rogue, drmario, columns, puyo and more). Underneath: the Track-A teaching carts (23-basics, 24-building-blocks, 25-patterns, 10b-camera, 06b-chords), filterenv's MONO legato Model-D voice, RAILS window-fill sizing, and stale-doc-check.js.

eras.title: Instrument racks, real multiplayer, and 3D back on the phone
eras.blurb: A monster day on three fronts. Music: a wave of instrument carts ships. acidrack is the RB-338 rack — two 303s plus a real 909 and curated 808, an FX strip, per-device effects, per-voice TUNE/DEC/CHAR knobs, and a seeded generator with a song code and WAV export. tracker is a Song→Chain→Phrase tracker in the LSDJ/M8 lineage (four tracks, mnemonic FX riding note_*, a random-song generator). yachtrack is the SESSION DESK that opens the yacht radio into an editable rack — tinyjam rack #2, the first chord-first rack and the first radio→rack seed handoff, locked to a 44-pair golden corpus. pocketbox is a buttons-only PGB-1 groovebox (p-locks, ratchets, conditions, a chord track, a ROLL-a-groove generator). delia is a concrete tape-kit that becomes the Radiophonic Workshop's increment 0, and otafamily is four otamatones over a gesture live-loop. The engine gains FILTER_DIODE — the real TB-303 diode-ladder squelch, with filter-spec.js as its acceptance oracle. Systems: multiplayer arrives for real — lockstep over UDP (rung 1) grows to LAN-by-IP, an engine-owned Host/Join/Solo boot lobby, LAN auto-discovery and a Winsock (.exe) port, all gated behind de_players() so solo carts stay clean — and the editor grows send-to-a-friend exports (.exe, a signed+notarized Mac .app via the new mac-app.sh, deploy-to-iPhone). And 3D comes back to the phone: sw_tritex gets a scan-box clamp and hoisted plot (infiniminer 1204→3.4ms, 358×), which on re-measurement overturns ADR-0024's no-3D-on-iOS call (podracer 89→6ms, infiniminer 10.9ms @59fps on an A13). Plus sloop's car↔foot seam (get out, walk, step into a house and the floor plan is real) and 26-first3d, the whole 3D pipeline on one spinning textured quad.

eras.title: The studio learns to ship
eras.blurb: The day the project grew a way out to the store. The engine seam lands first: de_switch_cart() gives every cart its own sound, video and sprite-sheet context — a config-request log recorded at drain and replayed on switch — so two carts run in one binary with zero edits, proven by the bundle-spike and hardened by ADR-0027 (cart-facing sound state flows ONLY through the request queue, the rule a bpm tempo-jump regression proved). On top of it, build-app.js turns an apps/<name>/app.json manifest into a multi-cart binary — a four-rung ladder from the dispatcher shim to a de:meta-fed launcher cart (tinyjam-menu) to a signed+notarized .app — and the same manifest builds and runs on iOS, in-app purchases and all (Spikes A + B). The umbrella app gets its name: Tiny Jam. Around the build sits a whole store pipeline, script-prepares-then-agent-decides by design (store-agents.md, over ADR-0026's in-house App Store Connect plan): the ASO lab — aso-research, aso-suggest, aso-lint, aso-compose, aso-brief and its aso-coverage mirror, and aso-score with a winnability check — plus store-shots (native frames → exact device screenshots), store-contact (a hero-frame contact sheet) and press-kit (a self-contained press page). The editor grows an Apps view that drives all of it. Two more threads open the same day: lay.h graduates from a layout vocabulary to a runtime library header and the device-adaptive-layout project kicks off (Phase 0 proven by rackfit's finger-sized reflow, Phase 1a's runtime canvas-dim globals landed), while build-app-reel.js and an in-editor trailer builder start turning a manifest into a demand-generating trailer.

eras.title: Carts that fit any glass, and a trailer to sell them
eras.blurb: Device-adaptive layout gets real. The framebuffer moves to the heap with a runtime stride and grows on demand (byte-identical to the old fixed path, so a de:meta resizable cart reflows to any size) — the editor ▶-run reflows it live, a harness --resize sweep exercises it, and Phase 2 lands iOS carts filling the device with safe-area insets and allowed rotation. Alongside it the in-editor trailer builder takes shape: per-clip trim + speed with a live visual preview, a drag-to-arrange timeline (add/remove/reorder/repeat), spec text cards with a magic-colour overlay grammar and a .reel @card syntax, an entrance vocabulary, a seamless loop-close transition, and beat-sync (breathe punches, boil ticks on the beat) — with the titlecard cart as its kinetic pixel-type slice 1 (boil + breathe, a full in/hold/out timeline with per-end effects). Underneath: raylib_compat stubs the window-size calls (GetScreenWidth/Height, SetWindowSize, ImageCrop), a DE_SHOW_SIZE overlay reads out live W×H, and welcome gets a leaner starter template and a new tagline.

eras.title: Record, replay, and the first lockstep handshake
eras.blurb: The editor learns to record and replay input tracks (.rec) — and the information-architecture seam it surfaces (where recorded media lives) opens the editor-media lane. The responsive work grows a gate: ui-audit gains a --resize sweep and a panel×size matrix, catches off-screen and overlapping widgets (not just text), and acidrack becomes the first rack to reflow (Phase 3 — landscape tabs, wrapping master knobs, content-aware tab thresholds). Netplay rung 5a begins and reaches code-complete in a day: the lockstep core compiles on web (a DE_NET_CORE/DE_NET_BUILD split, a transport seam, a non-blocking barrier and an echo fake-peer), then a WebSocket transport and a zero-dep relay — browser netplay code-complete. Around it the instrument museum map (the hub over every instrument doc) and a mic-and-sampling sketch get written, the design-system companion pages trace the evolution trail, and resolution-portable input tracks are reframed as an attract-mode IAP storefront.

eras.title: Multiplayer goes live, the repo splits, and a world draws its own roads
eras.blurb: The widest day of the week — four fronts at once. Multiplayer goes live — rung 5a is verified peer-to-peer, a Render relay is deployed and wss-verified, rooms are cart-scoped, and the site grows a play-together button and a room bar; a WebRTC P2P spike (rung 5b) then reaches Mac↔iPhone at ~12ms over wifi. The repo splits in two: site/ is untracked and the published gallery moves to its own public repo, this engine becomes dreamengine-studio, and publish-cart.sh grows two legs. The store lane pushes to TestFlight — Tiny Jam's bundle id is reserved on ASC, per-app icons stage through the manifest, and testflight.sh archives and uploads (v0.1 build live on ASC), with the iOS-26 SDK and SKTestSession wobbles logged. And a world starts generating itself: the worldgen ladder lands rungs 0–3 in one push — sndi-check (the street-network metric oracle) at rung 0, roadnet2's unified road_at() graph query (rung 1a) extracted to worldnet.h as the shared world spine (rung 1) the moment sloop became its second consumer, then citygrow's population-density field (rung 2) and per-city tensor-field arterials (rung 3), with the first generated-vs-real SNDi numbers measured. Plus the tr-606 drumatix, completing the Roland wing.

eras.title: Instruments reflow, a scale grid you can play, and the studio learns to promote
eras.blurb: The 101-commit day. Instrument UI learns to reflow: a device-matrix reference is written, and acidwire flips acidrack's layout through the whole device matrix with one key — rendering the real safe-area (notch/island/home-bar keep-outs), a real 303 step editor, per-instrument mute and patterns, a focus/fullscreen state and a desktop-fake-flipper-vs-device dual mode — while epianofit mocks the keybed's responsive layout, and the responsive-instrument-ui guide plus ADR-0028 (sensible defaults, optional tweaks) codify the playbook. Three instrument carts ship: scalegrid, a scale-locked isomorphic pad grid you actually play (11 scales, an OCT↔4TH row offset, SQR↔HEX Tonnetz packing with a nearest-centre hit-test, and VOICE and SIZE cycles, all pinned by a 71-assertion spec); newworld, a Joe Meek 'I Hear a New World' found-sound machine; and circlemachine, Raymond Scott's Circle Machine ring-sequencer. The studio learns to promote: asc-push.js pushes metadata/screenshots/IAPs to App Store Connect and marks promoted purchases (with a Store.swift PurchaseIntent), the leads marketeer maps a cart to its tribes and the venues where they gather (music coverage tuned to ~90%), and the editor's information architecture resolves into Make / Promote / Ship — a new per-cart Promote tab, with Dream as the zeroth verb closing the loop to a cycle. Netplay rung 5b (WebRTC P2P) is built, play-tested and published.

eras.title: The Promote tab ships, and one take fits every ratio
eras.blurb: The Promote tab ships end to end (A–E): every cart gets a place to bake a take into a clip, keep stills worth posting, and see its tribes and gallery link — playing back any take format — while the trailer builder and keyword research become scope-parameterized popups shared between a cart and an app, reels save and load per subject, and a cross-subject Reels overview tops the Apps page. The store lane finishes Tiny Jam's paperwork: the ☁︎ App Store push panel drives asc-push from inside the editor (the metadata channel, then promoted purchases), the listing copy and support URL land (metadata submission-complete), the IAP lineup gets cheap-tier prices and keyword-forward names, and two carts take trademark-safe display titles (Singing Stick, Strumharpy). Under it all ADR-0029 standardizes 320×200 as the base resolution and the 'one take, many ratios' thread cashes it in: an output-ratio picker (TikTok 9:16 / App Store / 16:9 / 1:1), per-ratio clip variants so reels fill the frame, crisp integer nearest-upscales, letterboxed exports for fixed carts — proven playable by the onetake cart. Plus chordblossom, a truthful homage to the Telepathic Instruments Orchid (chord types, voicings, modifiers, a following sub-bass that walks), the harness learning to record deterministically so a replay reconstructs the same world, and de:meta.slug anchoring every baked .cart.png back to its source .c.

eras.title: Grooveboxes, a supersaw primitive, and the engine cleans house
eras.blurb: Week 7 opens with grooveboxes and engine hygiene. motionbox arrives — an EMX-style motion sequencer built in slices: per-step parameter motion, a performance layer (part mutes, master DRIVE, swing), then the page axis — the same four knobs remapping per part × page, unlocking MOD and OSC pages without costing a row. tb303 grows the full sequencer (ties, octave up/down, pattern length, swing) and acidrack the full 16-voice 808. Mid-afternoon a wrong todo becomes a written lesson ('verify a claim by reading, not grepping') and then an engine primitive: instrument_unison, the first-class supersaw stack (ADR-0030), shown off by supersaw's JP-8000 detune-bloom lead with stereo WIDTH as a cart-land recipe on top. The engine-simplification backlog opens the same day and the dedup marathon begins — behaviour-preserving helper extraction across studio.c and sound.h (clamps, DC blockers, the SVF and ladder filter cores), each pass gated by the audio checks. Around the edges: hint(), an auto-fit control footer swept across 18 carts; the sprite editor learns PNG + Aseprite import/export; netplay gets Windows DPI/lobby fixes and net-health diagnostics; the harness learns scriptable held-mouse drags; and field-note 019 names the loop the studio now closes — Dream / Make / Show / Sell.

eras.title: Drive the city you grew
eras.blurb: The biggest day in a week, and the day the worldgen ladder pays off. citygrow lands rungs 4 and 5 in a morning: district faces extracted from the arterial graph, each face filled with one of five street morphs (grid, organic, cul-de-sac, superblock) picked by density, the whole city stitched and gated — T-junction share climbs from 1.1% to 64.6%, real Dutch-city territory — then a calibration pass puts five SNDi metrics dead-on against Rotterdam and sndi-check --compare turns the loop into a real PASS/FAIL gate. The grammar is extracted to citygen.h, given a road_at query seam, and by mid-afternoon sloop's M key drops the rig into a generated city — streets with grip, then buildings (rung 7) lining arterials and minors alike, colliding on their real orientation. In parallel the junction grammar completes Track B: roadkit.h extracts streetlab's curb-return geometry (B2) and N-arm field renderer (B3a) byte-identically, citydrive draws curb-return junctions through it in ground metres (J), and the interchange grammar (the ramp splines + rk_make_junction, B4) lets citygrow render rung 6's grade-2 nodes as real cloverleafs — with circ_capped fixing the 1.3-second zoom-ring stall the new I key exposed. The instrument shelf grows fmbox (an all-FM percussion groovebox with per-step p-locks and probability trigs), wavecandy (a five-view analyzer — spectrum, waterfall, scope, meters, and a vectorscope on the new scope_read2 stereo tap), and portapop's first three phases (the recordable seam and take model, multitrack + console, castable bass/drums/Rhodes). And the editor closes its oldest workflow gaps: a save-to-source button writes Code-tab edits back to the cart's .c (Gap 1), sprite-patch ships the pixel round-trip (Gap 2), slugs are backfilled across every cart, a flight recorder captures each editor run for keep-to-clips, and disclose.h + finger_px() (R2 + R3) give responsive racks a shared disclosure model and a real, device-verified finger unit.

eras.title: A distortion lab, and a day spent fixing what shipped
eras.blurb: acidrack grows a Devil Fish DEEP page (tb303 parity), per-303 reverb sends and a drive-mode waveshaper button (SOFT/HARD/FOLD/ASYM, all four A/B-verified distinct). distortion-lab starts as a design doc and by evening is a real growable cart: distlab climbs its own ladder in one sitting — Rung 0 (one drive stage on a held acid drone + a live transfer curve + a scope_read oscilloscope), Rung 1 (a PRE-EQ → DRIVE → POST-EQ tone stack on the master insert chain), Rung 2 (a cascaded second drive stage), Rung 3 (CRUSH + TAPE destruction combos), and a spectrum view (an in-cart 2048-pt FFT ported from wavecandy so you SEE the harmonics the distortion generates). glyphpup arrives — frameless glyph-puppet animation, three animals from one shared 6×6 glyph bank. Then the honest half of the day: a long bug-fix sweep across the shelf — an invisible catchstar spawned under the HUD, doom's gun latching after one shot, puyo sinking into the floor then snapping back, pitfall re-grabbing the rope instantly, outrun's flickering roadside trees, calgames' unplayable half-pipe — the kind of day that adds no features, just stops the ones you have from lying.

eras.title: A field guide to the engine, and a safety audit
eras.blurb: The book lands — 'Learn You a dreamengine for Great Good!', an illustrated Learn-You-a-Haskell-style field guide to the studio.h API whose every illustration is real harness output (so it can't drift), written start to finish in a day: fifteen chapters, a whole playable game by chapter 5, a webm you can hear by chapter 7, through touch/phone and ship-it at 15. The engine-simplification marathon closes 33/33 — behaviour-preserving dedup across net.h (handshake packets), ui.h (a shared button core + widget hash) and radio.h, each pass gated by the audio checks. Then a runtime-safety-audit reads the C and headers for real correctness and memory bugs and fixes eleven: a sprite-atlas OOB read, an audio-thread effect-index OOB, an untrusted network-frame OOB write that could kill a session, capped json recursion, degenerate-input guards across half the shared headers. The voice-debugging tools (--solo-slot stem render + a voice-allocation trace) get made discoverable, and acidrack grows a live bipolar DJ filter and 909 drum reverb.

eras.title: The device-face paradigm, and a shared physics toolkit
eras.blurb: Two ideas that reshape the shelf arrive the same day. The device-face paradigm — a reusable deep-instrument UI shape where one machine fills the screen and the knobs edit the selected step (parameter locks) — is prototyped in acidface and written down, with chordblossom/more-note-bass/pocketbox as worked faces and an OP-1 device analysis sharpening it. And physics.h: a tiny shared Verlet toolkit (PhysPt + phys_integrate/link/collide/aim) extracted from the carts that had each rolled their own — tombola builds its balls on it, then linerider, coaster, tentacle (a bone-driven textured mesh) and jelly (pressurized soft-body blobs that stack) all migrate onto it, the math verified byte-identical. The sampler grows real PCM sampling (a capture ring + INSTR_SAMPLE + movable chops, playback modes, a 16-step SONG mode, whole-song GRIT), drumkit.h ships the shared playable kit, pianoroll becomes a scrubbable roll you record and reshape, the floorplan cart gains an in-cart plan picker over a fetch-bridge, and reddit-gaps is born — the demand-discovery tool that mines a tribe's public RSS for what to build next.

eras.title: Rigid bodies, a control vocabulary, and the candy rack
eras.blurb: The biggest day of the week — around 118 commits, on four fronts. Box2D v3 gets vendored (pure C, per-target build) and wired in opt-in, and four physics carts prove it: tumble (a rigid-body slingshot with a 306-crate stress test and a wrecking ball on a chain), buggy (a hill-climb car on wheel joints), silverball (pinball on motored joints), and waterjar — a code-first PBD/SPH fluid on physics.h that ends the day as a dithered metaball liquid you can slosh into a curl. A control-vocabulary study opens and fills out in an afternoon: rotaries, switches, indicators, pads, faders, labels and grooveface, all in a beveled-lo-fi look with a one-source top-left (Win95) lighting rule and three swappable skins — the visual language the device-faces will speak. The acid voice family gets extracted to shared headers — acid303.h (both voicings from one file), then tr808.h and tr909.h (faithful voice banks, the acid303 move made for drums) — and on top of them acidcandy is born: the candy rack, a five-face device-face instrument (two 303s, a real blue 808 grid, an amber 909, an MST master face) firing on one shared transport, with a 303 bassline you draw as fat note-bars and a flag palette (ACC/SLD/TIE/OCT/LEN) you paint on. tombola becomes the OP-1 physics sequencer (note-balls tumbling in a spinning drum), and cart-collections lands — doc-anchored cross-cutting research threads.

eras.title: The candy rack gets its hands
eras.blurb: A quieter day spent making acidcandy feel played, not configured. The 303 roll learns to visualize its own flags — slides drawn as glide lines between pitches, ties as held continuation bars, octaves as up/down ticks, accents brighter — and note entry goes fluid: free-draw the melody by dragging (finger height = scale-snapped pitch, the bottom band erases in the same stroke), and paint-drag a flag across cells once the first cell decides place-or-remove. The MST face gains a drawable pattern-controlled-filter lane (acidrack parity), the drums get drag-paint and a DEEP knob page, and a nasty drag-release bounce that had been silently muting machines mid-playtest gets pinned and fixed — a stray second button-down landing on a mute LED about 8 frames after a lift, caught by a deterministic .rec replay. F5 runs the cart. reddit-gaps grows SFX, sound-toy and groovebox topics.

eras.title: It runs on Android, and the engine learns to hear
eras.blurb: Two frontiers open. Android becomes a real build target — spike 0 proves the engine renders on an arm64 emulator, then the host shell scaffold clears render/audio/touch (spikes 1–3), persistence wires up (spike 4), the build produces both arm64 and armv7 so any phone sideloads the APK, and the editor's share popover grows a 🤖 export-.apk button beside iPhone / .exe / mac. And the audio-input frontier: a mic-spike probe confirms LIVE — the engine hears (webcam mic, −17 dBFS) — and a Tier-1 microphone INPUT seam lands with a desktop backend and a mictest cart. Around them voxroll (a Melodyne-style vocal roll — draggable vowel-blobs on INSTR_VOICE, formant decoupled from pitch, glide on touch), tweenlab (a GSAP-style tween lab, seven rooms with a spec), extrudetext (a Hotline-Miami block-letter extrude lab), and acidcandy consolidating its levels onto the MST mixer and going landscape-safe.

eras.title: The mic pays off — voice becomes an instrument
eras.blurb: The day the audio-input frontier explodes. sample_autotune() lands as an engine primitive — formant-preserving pitch correction — and a whole auto-tune family grows on top: hardtune (the robot T-Pain flavour), mictune rebuilt as a focused auto-tune app, and transparent-autotune's offline PSOLA spike PASSES a real-voice check (the formants stay put) before autotune_mic takes it live the following day — streaming PSOLA on the audio thread, phase-locked WSOLA-style to kill the pulse. The mic becomes playable in more ways: singsynth (play your own voice as a synth, an honest SK-1), humseq (hum a melody and loop it back on any instrument), and vocoder v2 (an unvoiced/sibilance noise band so consonants cut through). Meanwhile chordblossom2 forks off as a genre-flavor chord-bloom rack — a Flavor table (bossa, yacht, citypop) driving a diatonic KEY mode where the keys ARE the flavor's chords, a SPICE strip and RICHNESS control, and a living accompaniment that breathes over a 4-bar phrase. And acid-pets arrives — petkit (a parametric reactive squishy shape atom), peteyes (an eye-emotion machine wired to scalar levers), and acidpets rolling boiled dot-eyes, cheeks and brows onto every machine's pet, each driven by its own state.

eras.title: A walking bass, a breathing band, and the arc bookkept
eras.blurb: walkbox is built — a TB-303-style walking-bass sequencer on the upright pizz voice, with a drawable velocity lane, a tabbed VEL|LEN lane (per-step note length + a staccato gate, TIE folded in) and a SWING knob to shuffle the odd 16ths into the pocket. chordblossom2 keeps growing — a flavor-aware GROOVE (sparse/normal/busy, the rhythm twin of RICHNESS), a tiny per-part pedalboard on the FX tab, a STOP that actually stops and a REST to hush the chord. autotune_mic gets its phase-lock epochs and a smoothed period, DE_MIC_WAV teaches the harness to feed a WAV in as the microphone (headless mic-cart testing), and the audio-input arc gets bookkept — vocoder v2 and offline auto-tune done, the live path parked for feel.

eras.title: The candy rack gets a name, a price, and a screen that fits
eras.blurb: acidcandy becomes a product. It is renamed Tiny Acid Jam, priced ($1.99, paid, one-time), given a 1024² App Store icon, fitted with a subtitle that actually fits the field (the acid→house swap ran 31/30, so the ampersand went), and pushed to App Store Connect. Around the naming, the engine finally stops fighting the glass: resizable carts FILL the window by fractional cover instead of integer letterboxing (the black border is gone), safe_rect learns to rescale its insets to the current canvas so a self-resizing cart stops getting a fat purple border AND stops clipping the notch, and build-app.js auto-enables DE_RESIZABLE when every cart in a manifest opts in. iOS gets on-device fill, a landscape lock, and a fixed resize-mid-frame crash. The day also writes down what all that reflow work has been circling: canvas-density-spectrum.md says scale and reflow are not two strategies but one dial, with ARRANGEMENT (the breakpoint) as an orthogonal axis. New carts: dubjam (a dub-techno rack, GREN filterbank plus a p-locked 808), morphbox (a morphing drum synth where 808 and 909 are one knob), ribbonpad (an MPE-style expressive pad), aquapuss (riding echo_insert_bbd, a new bucket-brigade voicing for the echo insert).

eras.title: Eight ways to lay out a 303, and harmony becomes a shared brain
eras.blurb: The densest design day in weeks, and almost none of it is code first. acidwide ships EIGHT draw-only arrangements of a single unhidden 303 (A through H) — a control rail, a full knob row, a chunky step strip, a tappable pitch-grid, the unpaged 303 with the flag palette as a persistent rail, then the alignment-preserving version where a horizontal mode-bar keeps grid and strip on one shared 16-column register, then the paged one where in-screen tabs swap the content. Only after those eight does the practice get written down (responsive-first-device-face.md's layered plan, L0 engine → L1 starter → L2 widgets → L3 grammar → L4 default) and then built: deviceface as the fork-me starter, cell-sized widgets plus the LayLane column register in ui.h/lay.h, and face.h as the grammar that declares zones and enforces the rules, proved the same day on chipjam, dubjam and grooveface. In parallel the harmony work goes from brief to shelf: harmony-brain.md is researched, harmony.h is extracted out of bossa and cocktail, and chordwise makes it BIDIRECTIONAL — analyze a progression, not just generate one. Also: the 303 realism pack (continuous resonance plus analog drift, a non-destructive classic⟷Devil-Fish voicing flag, an opt-in PolyBLEP band-limited saw with the raw one still default), drive_voice's dirt spectrum (Tube Screamer, RAT, Big Muff) with a cart each, reverb_spring's stretched-allpass dispersion and BOING knob, and lever #2's last mile — ADR-0033 plus youtube-push.js (recipe → 9:16 Short → upload) and dress-clip.js (hand-typed text burned into the letterbox bars in the real engine font).

eras.title: Eleven modes, a band that plays them, and a song machine takes shape
eras.blurb: The harmony brain grows up in a day. chordwise goes from three styles to eleven modes (major, minor, blues, dorian, then the other church modes) with genre style tables behind them, and grows a playable voicing rack, a genre-aware bassline voice-led through radio.h, a drumkit.h rhythm section with genre fills, a melody layer, FEEL (genre comp rhythm and off-beat swing) and live in-place chord editing you can do while it plays. modaljazz becomes the first radio station that GENERATES over a mode rather than replaying a written progression. Then bandbox: a 160×100 device-face mockup in the morning (a glass five-lane tracker, look pass only), a build brief by lunchtime, and a wired chord-chart sequencer with real harmony, a genre band and per-cell p-locks by the end of the day — plus GarageBand-style musical typing, an in-place lane editor, richer bass and drum p-lock vocabularies, tone selectors per voice, and three radio-idea genres. The second-customer rule fires twice: chordwise and bandbox both wanting the same tables is what starts the band.h conversation.

eras.title: A song format, a volta lock, and a pedalboard you plug a guitar into
eras.blurb: bandbox stops being a sequencer and becomes a song machine. The radio-idiom p-lock sweep mines 19 new per-cell locks out of the radio carts' actual bar moves (chord ANTIC/STAB/HELD/TACET, bass APPR/POP/GHOST/PEDAL, drum HALF/OPEN/HATS/DOUBLE, band FEEL HUSH/STOP/LIFT) — ANTIC anticipating forward-only and later learning to tie over the barline, LIFT as the truck-driver gear change. Then a SONG button with a versioned save format where one 120-byte blob is both the autosave and the demo shape, then the VOLTA lock generalizing 1st/2nd endings over a four-round cycle in two families (gate WHEN a bar sounds, or gate its LOCKS), format v2, and demos to show it off: CITY POP built through the UI on the Royal Road, then NAPOLEON as a four-round disco-funk form. spec grows 112 → 131 green through it. Meanwhile a whole washy-hats hunt gets fixed with numbers rather than taste (open-hat role a velocity notch softer, everything that densifies the hat line moved to the closed hat, then real hat CHOKES so a new open kills the last: −0.2 → −3.0 dB across the groove window) and the crash gets ducked at the mixer once vel tweaks measured worth only ~1 dB. And the mic reaches the pedal tier: input_monitor() routes the live mic through the master fx chain, micfuzz proves it, pedalboard grows GUITAR IN so you play a real guitar through a chain you built, and it becomes the second app — Tiny Pedal Board, with an icon, screenshots, a listing and a price. Three iOS mic-host gotchas get found and fixed on the way (the mic was killing the whole app's output).

eras.title: The tablet rack replaces the old one, and physics gets a shelf
eras.blurb: A day of one long climb and one new frontier. The iPad ROOMY layout goes from mockup to THE tablet view in about forty commits — shared-screen soft-keys, 2-wide knob grids, a Devil Fish deep page, pattern banks, a walking playhead, tab-and-band screen reorgs for both the 303 and the drums, PERF lenses, MUT/REC latches, per-step p-locks, tap-a-lane-label-to-expand, and a maker look pass on the colours from his own pico32 swatch — and then the old 2×2 rack is deleted rather than kept as an option. The other half of the day opens Box2D properly: six carts plus boxrig.h as the shelf (sprite alpha → hull, tritex the polygon from its own verts, verlet↔rigid coupling), a physics playground, and puppets you can grab. Also acidtheremin, and lab-experiments.md writing down the try-before-commit LAB pattern chordblossom2 had been using — flip a seam live, decide by ear.

eras.title: A quiet weekend, then the post-hardware rack
eras.blurb: The first real lull of the project (12, 2 and 21 commits across Friday to Sunday, against nine weeks that routinely cleared 100) and it goes on hygiene and one new idea. Friday greens the gates and finds a genuine render gotcha — coverage fills and line() outlines drift against each other, so an oriented box outlined with line() feet past its own fill, which had bitten boxjelly twice. Saturday names a workflow: 'update mipolai website' becomes the trigger phrase for the personal-site pass. Sunday builds the post-hardware genre rack: contemporary-rebirth.md argues that what a modern genre needs is TECHNIQUES, not more machine emulations, and cashes it out immediately — multiband() lands as 3-band dynamics with an upward half (the OTT box) with hyperbox as its hyperpop showcase, then sample_shift() and harmonize_mic() as the INTERVAL face of the autotune PSOLA. Then the popping hunt: two attempts at phase-locking the PSOLA epochs both regress the snap face into period doubling and both get reverted, Rubber Band 4.0 is read as a reference (GPL, so a reference and not a dependency) and one cheap objection to its two-stage claim is tested and refused, and the round ends by building psola-check.js — three detectors, because each is blind to a defect the others catch — which kills a third epoch attempt in one command.

eras.title: An outside text audits the whole engine
eras.blurb: hyperbox iterates hard (v2 through v4: boxes that reward being opened, one keybed instead of phantom keys, drums you play rather than program) and then the biggest research push in the repo starts. The engine is cross-checked against Gordon Reid's Synth Secrets — 63 monthly parts, a 335-page compiled PDF the owner supplied — in eight passes over one day: brass, strings, plucked strings, pianos, drums, flutes, the Hammond, and the effects layer. The sieve comes out COMPLETE, with roughly 106 sub-findings, one correction to the audit's own earlier claim (Reid contradicts himself between Part 10 and Part 47 and explicitly retracts the earlier one), one section where the engine turns out to get physics right that is easy to get backwards, and one open design question worth more than most of the findings: every patch in the book is subtractive and all our imitative engines are physical models, so we may be missing a category rather than mistranslating one. Then the research output becomes a work list — synth-secrets-plan.md turns the findings into one ordered ledger with an explicit rule for how an item is judged done (the owner's ear, on a cart where you can hear it) and a rule for recording DROPs. Phase 0 runs ten fact fixes and five measurements, four of which changed the plan — and then, the same day, Phase 1 starts paying out: solina's detune ladder, the 808 cymbal's three unequal decays, a snare that answers how hard you hit it on both machines, the layered piano (which is also where two dead sliders got found), and 1.4 recorded as a DROP because Reid loses all three of his brass envelope numbers. Five of seven items, shipped and judged, on the day the sieve finished. Alongside it: icon-mask.js, which measures the App Store icon mask out of Apple's own renderer and reports which of your pixels get cut, and FONT_TIC.

eras.title: Phase 1 ships by ear, and a crowd of ragdolls learns to stand
eras.blurb: Phase 1 closes. Five of its items had shipped the day before; today Part 51's two loudness→brightness tricks land in martenot and that is 7 of 7 — with 1.4 brass and 1.6 Hammond recorded as DROPs rather than quietly skipped, which is the plan's stated rule working as intended. Each shipped item kept its old sound on a toggle and none of them landed on a measurement alone; the owner had to hear it first. Two engine gaps close as real API: instrument_keytrack() so the filter can follow the keyboard at last, and ENV_CUTOFF_OCT / LFO_CUTOFF_OCT so a filter sweep's depth is stated in octaves. mono.h arrives as the note-priority and trigger-policy header, and promoting it immediately confesses a bug in sh101 (PORTA OFF meant 0 ms, so the new trigger modes were gliding anyway). The audit also produces its first bug of the invisible kind: instrument_mode rejected two of its own indices, so two finished piano sliders had never worked. And martenot's morph turns out to have been CRACKLING, with two causes and one new oracle (click-check.js) to see it. In the other window, boxhuman goes from one figure to five builds off one rig table — scale and girth rather than five copies, then per-build rest poses so they are five attitudes rather than five bodies, a fidget through the joints rather than the render, a stance, and finally H, where the crowd goes up on its hands.

eras.title: The engine gets its inharmonicity, and then the project audits its own records
eras.blurb: Phase 2's hard half, and it is mostly a story about being wrong in public. The piano's dispersion cascade is found feasible but with the coefficient's SIGN wrong rather than its scale; step 2's compensation and dispersion turn out not to be separable; the owner's ear kills an A/B and is right (it was confounded by DECAY, not timbre); and the resolution records that both failures were the agent's own, in the test rig. It ships as MODE_PIANO_STIFF with the design commitment that inharmonicity stays swappable, the completed Railsback curve, and a tune-check that now ASSERTS the stretch curve instead of tolerating it. 2.3(b) is DROPPED on the owner's call and the ranking lesson is kept as the valuable part. BOWED gets the body it never had, opt-in and off by default, and then loses MODE_BOW_BODYTYPE because one body and one knob is the honest surface. Three more engine seams land (note_retrig for re-articulating a held voice, note_glide's ms finally meaning milliseconds via a fixed-duration ramp, then a glide SCALE dial when the switch could not reach the best setting) plus mouse_wheel_x() and stereo-check.js, the oracle for the half of the signal every other audio gate throws away at the door. pedalboard gets a twenty-commit polish marathon that keeps finding controls that were lying (autopan's SPD buried its useful range past 4 Hz, WAV picked from 8 LFO shapes and never said which, a muted string was fret 0 so every power chord had a third in it). And then the sweep nobody had done: canvas-diff's golden had been red for 20 days because nobody ran it (now wired into repo-doctor), HANDOFF.md is cut from 1356 to 649 lines and 19 lanes to 13 to 9 — moving the seven facts that existed nowhere else OUT before deleting anything — handoff.js's own back door is audited and found to be guarding three holes, and status-check.js is born for the ledger that everything told you to trust and nothing held to a standard. It immediately finds that 20 of 53 'open' items had already shipped.

markedDays.2026-07-22: The song-machine day — 88 commits. bandbox gains the 19-lock radio-idiom vocabulary, a versioned SONG format where one 120-byte blob is both autosave and demo, and the VOLTA lock (1st/2nd endings generalized over a four-round cycle), with spec climbing to 131 green. The washy-hats hunt gets settled with measurements rather than taste (−0.2 → −3.0 dB across the groove window, then real hat chokes). And the mic reaches the pedal tier: input_monitor() runs the live mic through the master fx chain, so pedalboard grows GUITAR IN and becomes the second app in review, Tiny Pedal Board.
markedDays.2026-07-23: Two frontiers in one day — the iPad ROOMY layout climbs from mockup to THE tablet view in ~40 commits and the old 2×2 rack is DELETED rather than kept as an option, while Box2D opens properly: six carts plus boxrig.h as the shelf, a physics playground and puppets you can grab.
markedDays.2026-07-26: The post-hardware rack — contemporary-rebirth.md argues a modern genre needs TECHNIQUES rather than more machine emulations, and cashes it out the same day: multiband() (the OTT box) with hyperbox as its showcase, then sample_shift() + harmonize_mic(). The PSOLA popping hunt fails twice in public (both phase fixes reverted) and ends by building the oracle that could see it, psola-check.js, which kills a third attempt in one command.
markedDays.2026-07-28: The sieve day — the engine is cross-checked against Gordon Reid's Synth Secrets, all 63 parts, in eight passes covering every instrument family and the effects layer. It comes out COMPLETE at ~106 sub-findings, including a correction to the audit's own earlier claim (Reid retracts himself between Part 10 and Part 47), one place the engine gets hard physics RIGHT, and the design question that outranks most of the findings: every patch in the book is subtractive and all our imitative engines are physical models. Then the findings become an ordered build plan with a stated rule for how an item is judged done — and for how a DROP is recorded.
markedDays.2026-07-29: Phase 1 complete, 7 of 7, every item shipped only once the owner could hear it — and two of the seven recorded as DROPs rather than skipped. instrument_keytrack() and the octave-denominated filter sweep land as real API, mono.h arrives and immediately confesses a bug in sh101, martenot's morph turns out to have been crackling (one new oracle, click-check.js), and instrument_mode is caught rejecting two of its own indices, which had left two finished piano sliders unreachable. Meanwhile boxhuman becomes five builds off one rig table and goes up on its hands.
markedDays.2026-07-30: The day the audit turned inward — 73 commits. The piano's inharmonicity ships as MODE_PIANO_STIFF after a run of public wrongness (the sign, not the scale; the compensation not separable; the owner's ear killing an A/B and being right; both failures the agent's own, in the test rig), BOWED finally gets a body, and note_retrig / note_glide / the glide scale dial / mouse_wheel_x / stereo-check all land. Then the sweep nobody had done: canvas-diff's golden had been red 20 days because nobody ran it, HANDOFF.md drops 1356 → 649 lines with the unique facts moved out FIRST, and status-check.js is born for the ledger everything said to trust — finding 20 of 53 'open' items already shipped.
